    Language / JugaadLang

    Functions and modules

    Functions give a name to reusable behavior. Modules group related behavior behind an import.

    Define and call a function

    Use banao to define a function and wapas to return a value. Arguments may have defaults.

    banao kul_daam(cup, daam=15):
    wapas cup * daam

bolo(kul_daam(3))
bolo(kul_daam(2, 20))

    Expected output:

    45
40

    Assignments inside a function normally create local variables. Pass data in and return results instead of relying on global state. Use sabka only when you intentionally need to assign a global name.

    Import a module

    Use lao for a module and se ... lao ... for a named import. JugaadLang resolves its standard library names and can import installed Python modules.

    lao ganit
se math lao sqrt
bolo(ganit.square(5))
bolo(sqrt(16))

    Expected output:

    25
4.0

    See the standard library for available modules. Third-party Python packages must be installed in the environment used by jug. For module resolution details, consult the architecture; do not assume a .jug file is automatically importable as a Python module.

    Classes

    Use ustad to define a class. The constructor is shuru, and khud refers to the instance.

    ustad Chai:
    banao shuru(khud, daam):
        khud.daam = daam

    banao bill(khud, cup):
        wapas khud.daam * cup

chai = Chai(12)
bolo(chai.bill(3))

    Expected output:

    36

    The syntax reference and keyword reference cover annotations, generators, and asynchronous keywords. Start with ordinary functions before introducing those features.
